summary:
Six source-bound proposal decisions: C3 customer inference and provider support remain unresolved. C3 mixed-content shared training and all three exact SAI operations are off under the supplied record. No operation qualifies for present enablement or a notice-only launch.

The strongest useful design keeps content inference with the properly licensed customer or genuine End Customer. It combines that route with content-free provider diagnostics and separate object-level licensed technology or Feedback improvement lanes. SAI contracting-Customer internal use cannot borrow the End Customer grant. C3 Feedback rights cannot absorb all workload content.

All controls remain false. Missing executed instruments, replaced exhibits, redactions and current applicability remain explicit. SAI same-source hierarchy and conflicting scopes appear in ENG1 and U9 because its source units share one document ID. This hypothetical public-sample export grants no actual customer clearance and changes no live account or feature.

engineering_outputs.body:

Proposed metric schema: device_fault_code, gpu_error_count, temperature_band, power_band, capacity_used and service_health. This schema is an engineering allowlist, not a claim that any real field already has permission. Exclude free text, command lines, payload fragments, paths with secrets, prompts, outputs and customer documents. Classify identifiers and timing data for confidentiality and Personal Data before use.

Distinguish provider-system telemetry from customer-uploaded workload logs by producer and field provenance. A provider-generated log cannot serve as a conduit for prohibited content capture. For SAI, section 8.2 permits specified use analysis but its content proviso remains binding. For C3, use only documentation and operational records with actual ownership and purpose authority.

A customer summary may enter support only after its concrete fields pass the applicable content, confidentiality and purpose checks. No external model provider or new subcontractor is part of this design. Source basis: E6–E9, E25–E26, E31–E36, E44–E45, E49–E53.
engineering_outputs.acceptance_criteria: A synthetic support bundle with a hidden prompt, document fragment or secret fails before model ingestion. Pure allowlisted metrics produce a useful hardware diagnosis in an isolated test. Customer Personal Data and mixed-origin logs cannot pass through a filename-based telemetry exemption. C3 content support remains unresolved and SAI content support remains off. Neither operation inherits enablement from the alternate metric route.

Respect the Customer Background IPR exception and any actual section 15.5 license predicate. Quarantine a mixed submission because sections 8.2 and 15.4 both contain broad override language. No universal de-identification, consent, model ownership or cross-customer permission is inferred. Source basis: E4–E9, E11, E13, E18–E19, E25–E26, E31–E38, E47 and E56.

For C3, implement section 9.4 return or deletion and officer certification with its exact exceptions. For SAI, preserve section 17.6 qualifications and section 17.5 continuing protection. Do not assume every weight is Confidential Information or that every weight is free of it. Assess copied or recoverable protected information and obtain a defensible disposition for affected model artifacts.

Use synthetic planted secrets for extraction tests. A failed extraction attempt is exposure evidence only, not proof of consent or irreversible anonymization. Do not use a backup-media schedule as authority for indefinite model retention. Source basis: E5–E9, E11, E35–E37 and E56.
engineering_outputs.acceptance_criteria: A simulated valid deletion request removes the targeted synthetic examples from active stores, caches and applicable copies. The receipt distinguishes completed deletion, retained licensed use, delayed backup expiry and unresolved derived-information questions.
